newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mismanagement alleged at Zimbabwe pension fund.
newsitem.headline: Mismanagement alleged at Zimbabwe pension fund.

text.p: A Zimbabwean government minister in charge of the southern African country's compulsory state pension fund alleged on Wednesday there was gross mismanagement at the fund.

Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Florence Chitauro said the "whole management" at the National Social Security Authority (NSSA) was to blame, and not just its Irish expatriate general manager Rory O'Shea as charged by some members of parliament.

"There is a lot of mismanagement. We have a situation where employees contributions lie idle in an officer's desk for seven months without banking or receipting," she told a management seminar for senior civil servants.
"And the officer even has the audacity to write to employers claiming that contributions have not been sent," she said.
NSSA was formed in 1994 amid fierce opposition from private and quasi-state pension funds who said the government was duplicating their work.

NSSA collects an average of Z$70 million (U.S.$6.3 million) in monthly contributions from Zimbabwean workers, but lately it has been accused by some MPs of profligate spending, including on wages and allowances for expatriate staff.
O'Shea was unavailable for comment on Wednesday, but has in the past denied the allegations.
The government has set up a parliamentary commission to investigate the charges.
